gaps.explanation: Detail = budgetary-basis schedules (General Fund p10 9,037,475; nonmajor special revenue pp14-20, Debt Service p21, Capital Project Funds pp22-23 = 8,829,630; total 17,867,105, every printed actual is in detail). Statement p5 (GAAP): General 9,205,397 + Other Governmental Funds 8,266,174 = 17,471,571. (1) General Fund: budgetary 9,037,475 (p10) vs GAAP 9,205,397 (p5) = -167,922 (different basis). (2) Nonmajor: budget schedules 8,829,630 vs GAAP Other Governmental Funds 8,266,174 = +563,456. By printed row: Taxes 2,257,649 vs Property Taxes 2,257,497 (+152); Other Taxes 3,972,552 vs Franchise 350,000 + Local Option Sales 3,603,731 (+18,821); Intergovernmental 1,732,963 vs 1,263,471 (+469,492); Charges 308,895 vs 272,155 (+36,740); Gain on sale of land 133,393 vs 83,430 (+49,963); Interest 24,013 vs 59,347 (-35,334); Rental 107,331 vs 89,235 (+18,096); Miscellaneous 289,426 (incl. County/LEC 141,963, which the same p15 schedule also prints as Transfers In 141,963) vs 203,802 (+85,624); Contributions 0 vs 65,098 (-65,098); Reimbursements 0 vs 15,000 (-15,000); sum +563,456; -167,922 + 563,456 = 395,534 = the gap. The Other Governmental Funds column also contains the South Sioux City Community Foundation fund, which has no budget schedule; its amounts (very likely the Contributions 65,098 and Reimbursements 15,000 that no schedule prints) are printed only on the nonmajor combining statement, which is not in this trim (FY2023/FY2024 trims include it at pp11-16). Re-trim with the FY2022 combining nonmajor statement to add the Community Foundation column; the rest is budgetary vs GAAP basis. No fix possible from the trimmed pages.

Statement p5: General 8,397,496 + Other Governmental Funds 5,499,967 = 13,897,463. Detail (budgetary): General Fund p10 8,325,108 (-72,388 vs GAAP) + nonmajor/debt/capital schedules pp14-23 5,636,167 (+136,200 vs Other Governmental Funds) = 13,961,275; -72,388 + 136,200 = 63,812 = the gap. Nonmajor by function, schedules vs p5: Public Safety 2,151,891 vs 2,164,653 (-12,762); Culture 1,306,896 vs 1,132,206 (+174,690); Community Development 299,457 vs 268,258 (+31,199); Capital Projects 1,034,007 vs 887,134 (+146,873); Debt Service 843,916 vs 1,047,716 (-203,800); sum +136,200. Part of the GAAP column is the South Sioux City Community Foundation fund (no budget schedule; FY2023 shows it with debt service 228,434 and community development), whose column is printed only on the nonmajor combining statement, not in this trim. Budgetary vs GAAP basis for the rest. No fix possible from the trimmed pages.

Statement p5 Transfers In 2,213,746 = General 74,242 + Other Governmental Funds 2,139,504. Detail transfers in = every printed budget-schedule actual: General 74,242 (p10), Capital Improvement Sales Tax 112,233 (p14), Fire 960,000 (p15), County/LEC 141,963 (p15), Miscellaneous Projects 486,703 (p23), Disaster Recovery 180,348 (p23) = 1,955,489. Nonmajor statement 2,139,504 - schedules 1,881,247 = 258,257 = the gap. The difference belongs to funds/transfers no budget schedule prints (the Community Foundation fund has no budget schedule; in FY2023 and FY2024 it receives Transfers In 228,434 each year, and the FY2022 CIST transfers out 938,434 exceed budget by 228,434, so 228,434 is probably the Foundation's; the remaining 29,823 equals the transfers_out gap, i.e. a transfer between nonmajor funds that the budget schedules do not show). The nonmajor combining statement that would print these per fund is not in the trim; cannot be confirmed or fixed from the trimmed pages.

Statement p5 Transfers Out 2,084,283 = General 141,963 + Other Governmental Funds 1,942,320. Detail transfers out = every printed budget-schedule actual: General 141,963 (p10), Capital Improvement Sales Tax 938,434 (p14), Riverfront TIF 112,233 (p16), Roth TIF 267,275 (p17), Wireless 911 74,242 (p19), Public Safety Sales Tax 250,000 (p20), Debt Service 270,313 (p21) = 2,054,460. Nonmajor statement 1,942,320 - schedules 1,912,497 = 29,823 = the gap; the same 29,823 is left over in transfers in after the probable Community Foundation 228,434, so it is an interfund transfer among nonmajor funds not printed on any budget schedule. The combining nonmajor statement (per-fund GAAP transfers) is not in the trim; cannot be fixed from the trimmed pages.
